exercises.prompt: In Classical Arabic prosody (al-ʿarūḍ), how is a doubled consonant (shaddah) treated during scansion?
choices: Written as two consonants: first vowelless (sukūn), second vowelled
Counted as a single short syllable
exercises.answer: Written as two consonants: first vowelless (sukūn), second vowelled
exercises.explanation: Prosodic writing (al-kitābah al-ʿarūḍiyyah) expands every shaddah into Cْ + Cَ so syllable length is measured accurately.

feedback.rule: Prosodic scansion writes all pronounced sounds: shaddah → CْCَ, tanwīn → نْ.

exercises.prompt: True or False: The classical meter al-Ṭawīl scans as فَعُولُنْ مَفَاعِيلُنْ فَعُولُنْ مَفَاعِيلُنْ in each hemistich.
exercises.explanation: True. Al-Ṭawīl alternates the 5-letter foot فَعُولُنْ with the 7-letter foot مَفَاعِيلُنْ.
